text.p: The European Parliament on Thursday adopted its position on future enlargement of the European Union, urging the Union not to take on new members rashly and to strengthen the EU first through institutional reforms.

Accepting a report by Greek European People's Party deputy Efthymios Christodoulou, the parliament said the Union should carefully weigh up the financial implications before enlargement, and should take particular care in the agricultural and structural funds areas.
The Christodoulou report said as part and parcel of the enlargement new members would have to accept economic and monetary union as an objective.
It throws doubt on whether the EU's current own resources ceiling of 1.27 percent -- above which the EU member states do not want to go -- will be sufficient to finance the enlargement.
The report said that the applicants should be obliged to go further in creating market economies, including pushing privatisation further and restructuring their public sectors.
